name: Raptor Head
summary: Across the Barrens, Raptor Head trophies answer a bounty from Gazrog at the Crossroads. The guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft.

sections.title: Bounty of the Crossroads
sections.body: A stolen chest of guard payroll has left the Crossroads watchtower without its silver. The defenders caught a wild raptor red-handed, to their disbelief. Gazrog has put a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators will be culled before they can pilfer more Horde supplies.

faq.q: Why does Gazrog want raptor heads?
faq.answer: A shipment of silver meant as payroll for the Crossroads guards was stolen from their tower in a chest. To everyone's disbelief, a raptor was caught in the act. Gazrog wants the beasts hunted across the Barrens so they cannot raid the settlement again.

faq.q: Why would wild raptors steal silver?
faq.answer: Gazrog admits he has no idea why wild beasts would want metal coins. Raptors in Kalimdor are notorious for their unnerving cunning, and the theft leaves the Crossroads guards embarrassed and eager for retribution.

Heads come from Sunscale raptors roaming the central and southern Barrens, including Sunscale Lashtails, Screechers, and Scytheclaws. Notorious beasts such as Ishamuhale and Takk the Leaper also yield heads.

faq.q: What happens after turning in the heads?
faq.answer: Once Gazrog receives twelve heads and the raptor menace is thinned, attention turns to tracking down where the stolen silver shipment was actually taken.

angles.text: The Crossroads is the heart of Horde travel in central Kalimdor. Clearing the thieving predators secures the garrison's supplies and payroll.
Tracking Sunscale raptors across the Barrens' dry scrub tests your skill against some of the savannah's most aggressive and cunning pack hunters.
